aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

monthly_review.summary: July shows clear aerobic progression: faster pace, higher HR, more Z3–Z4 work, and improved efficiency — but cadence dropped and aerobic TE rose slightly, suggesting emerging fatigue or pacing inconsistency.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite running 5.2 km less and 3 fewer sessions, average pace improved by 20 sec/km while average HR increased — indicating meaningful aerobic sharpening, confirmed by VO2max rising +3.0 from baseline and recent best 10k effort (5070s).

goal_tracker.message: You need 5.2 km across ~3 sessions in the next 10 days to match last month’s volume — but given chronic sleep debt (<7h for 15 of last 14 days) and low training readiness (17/100), chasing this number risks compromising aerobic gains. Prioritize quality over quantity: 1x easy 5 km run + 2x short recovery runs (≤3 km, HR <130) is safer and more productive.

insights.title: Sleep debt correlates with reduced running economy
insights.body: Recent sleep avg is 4.3h (15/14 days <7h), and the latest running economy value is 262.2 ml O2/kg/km — the highest in the recent 6-run series (median = 253.9). Poor sleep impairs neuromuscular coordination and metabolic efficiency, likely contributing to the +8.3 ml/kg/km jump from median.

insights.title: ACWR of 0.7 reflects underloading — but decoupling remains unstable
insights.body: ACWR is low (0.7), signaling detraining risk, yet aerobic decoupling median is 6.66% (well above 5% threshold), and latest value is only 0.84% — an outlier likely enabled by the long 14.1 km run at very low intensity (9:22 min/km, HR 141). This suggests decoupling is highly pace- and fatigue-dependent, not yet robust across intensities.

insights.title: Strong HRV masks underlying fatigue expressed in stride metrics
insights.body: HRV is elevated (+3.3 ms vs baseline), yet vertical oscillation rose from 7.5 to 8.5 cm (7/6–7/6 to 7/6–7/21), ground contact time dropped from 322 to 300 ms, and stride length swung wildly (70.4 → 89.8 → 70.4 cm). This mismatch signals compensatory movement patterns — likely due to sleep debt overriding autonomic resilience.

insights.title: Zone 3 delivers best efficiency per heartbeat — but volume there is rising unsustainably
insights.body: Efficiency-by-zone shows Z3 = 0.7508 m/beat (highest among zones >Z2), yet Z3 % jumped from 19% (May) to 26% (July) — coinciding with rising aerobic TE (+0.3) and declining cadence (-5 spm). This suggests early signs of neuromuscular strain in the 'aerobic threshold' zone, where efficiency gains are most sensitive to fatigue.

recommendations.action: Every night: Sleep protocol — lights out by 22:00, no screens after 21:30, 15-min guided breathing before bed (aim for ≥5.5h sleep tracked via Garmin)
recommendations.reason: Chronic sleep deficit is the dominant limiter: 4.3h avg directly undermines running economy, decoupling resilience, and recovery balance sustainability

risk_flags.action: Replace one midweek run with mobility + barefoot drill session; monitor stride consistency daily

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize movement consistency over speed or distance — using cadence, stride length, and vertical oscillation as real-time biofeedback to rebuild coordination eroded by sleep debt.
